synopsis: The ISO 18497-1–4:2024 family provides agricultural off-road obstacle-protection standards and is described as a close cousin of the heavy off-road collision-mitigation function under study [f1099, f7190]. Its scope covers machine design principles, obstacle-protection design principles, and verification methods including test objects; the corpus calls it the nearest published example of an off-road sector incorporating perception test objects into a standard [f450, f451]. Parts 1–4 were published in July 2024, with the planning chapter specifically identifying Parts 1, 2 and 4 as replacing ISO 18497:2018 [f7187, f9763]. Despite this relevance, the review of Parts 1, 2 and 4 did not find a minimum-method table, so the corpus does not establish such a table as available for planning validation [f9765].

relations.note: Both report July 2024 publication; the planning chapter names three parts and their predecessor.
Adds design principles and verification methods to the agricultural obstacle-protection scope.
Inclusion of test objects supports the characterization as a published off-road perception-testing precedent.
Agricultural off-road obstacle protection explains its relevance to heavy off-road collision mitigation.
Design and verification coverage supports the family's relevance to the function under study.
Qualifies verification-method coverage: reviewers did not see a minimum-method table in three parts.
